chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he said the Takbir in prayer, he raised his hands until they nearly reached his ears.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّكْبِير: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar', specifically the opening Takbir in prayer

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq raise his hands during the Takbir of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the physical etiquette (adab) of the opening Takbir, specifically the raising of hands (raf' al-yadayn) to the level of the ears. In Shia jurisprudence, this detail underscores the importance of following the Prophet’s and Imams’ precise physical movements during prayer, distinguishing it from other schools that may raise hands only to the shoulders or keep them still. The report serves as a practical guide for worshippers to emulate the prophetic model of humility and focus at the commencement of Salah.
